abstract:
A null vector, nonzero but with square zero, can never be divided by, even inside a larger algebra. [[c:transport.noinverse]] With both space and time directions and at least three dimensions, no choice of partial inverses respects the symmetries, however the algebra is enlarged. [[c:transport.no-go-level-elements]]

The fix is a larger space with one new positive and one new negative direction, $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$. [[c:transport.minimality]] This becomes a recipe sorting every failure of division into three kinds, each with its own fix. [[c:transport.transport-algorithm]] Each step up the resulting tower adds exactly one fermionic mode. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]]

At the centre of a non-rotating black hole the obstruction is the kind this repair supplies. [[c:singularity.type-n-only-type-n]] Einstein's vacuum equations become one null tractor staying constant. [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]] The boundary modes carry a thermal state at the Hawking temperature, the only quasi-free state thermal for the boost clock. [[c:hawking.i-state]]

On the matter side, the smallest massive twistor composite carries exactly the symmetry of the strong, weak and hypercharge forces. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]] With an assumed hierarchical second correction, the neutrino masses add up to about 0.059 eV. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]] Given stated symmetry assumptions, a mirror world copies the Standard Model. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]]
introduction:
This tour follows one idea from pure algebra all the way to particles, neutrinos and dark matter. [[t]] It starts with a failure of division, because every later step is a response to that failure. [[t]]

It then shows how enlarging the space repairs the failure, and applies the repair to geometry and gravity, then to black holes and heat, and last to matter. [[t]] The assumptions that some results rest on are gathered first, under their own heading, so that what is proved stays separate from what is supposed. [[t]]
i:zero-divisors:
The series starts from a simple question: what happens when you try to divide by something that is not zero but whose square is zero? [[t]]

In a space of mixed signature, $pq \neq 0$, like the spacetime of relativity, such vectors exist, and they form a cone much like a light cone. [[c:transport.existence-locus-type-n]]
t:^>transport.noinverse:
The first result shows how firmly these vectors resist division. [[t]]

A null $v \neq 0$ has no inverse on either side, in $\Cl(p,q)$ or in any larger algebra containing it. [[c:transport.noinverse]]
t:transport.noinverse>transport.no-go-le:
With exact inverses ruled out, one might settle for partial ones. [[t]]

A partial inverse $\sigma(v)$ satisfies \[ v\,\sigma(v)\,v = v \] but in mixed signature with $n \geq 3$ no choice of one for each null $v$ is equivariant, even under $\Spin^0(p,q)$, in any extension. [[c:transport.no-go-level-elements]]
i:clifford-structure: A Clifford algebra is built from a space of directions together with a rule for multiplying them. [[c:conformal.blade-basis-persists-under-degeneracy]] Before trying to repair these algebras, it helps to know what they really are. [[t]]
t:transport.no-go-level-elements>transpo:
The classical answer is a short and complete list. [[t]]

Each real Clifford algebra is a matrix algebra over $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$, or a sum of two, according to the residue \[ d \equiv p - q \pmod 8 \] and it is simple except when $p - q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$. [[c:transport.classification-real-clifford-algebras]]
i:completion: Since division cannot be rescued inside the algebra, the series moves outside it, into a larger space. [[t]] The question for this section is how much larger that space must be, and what to do once one is there. [[t]]
t:transport.classification-real-clifford:
The first answer concerns the reciprocal of a single vector. [[t]]

The larger space needs one new direction of each sign, \[ \Cl(p,q) \;\longrightarrow\; \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1) \] and this hyperbolic plane is enough and unique up to isometry. [[c:transport.minimality]]
t:transport.minimality>conformal.minimal:
A similar count applies when the geometry itself is degenerate. [[t]]

A radical of dimension $r$ needs $r$ new partners, so $\Cl(p,q,r)$ embeds minimally in $\Cl(p{+}r, q{+}r)$. [[c:conformal.minimal-nondegenerate-completion]]
t:conformal.minimal-nondegenerate-comple:
These pieces now fit together into one working procedure. [[t]]

The theorems distil into a six-step procedure, and every step names the theorem that licenses it. [[c:transport.transport-algorithm]]
i:tower:
Repeating the basic repair builds a tower of ever larger spaces. [[t]]

Each step adds a null pair $v_i, w_i$, and these obey exactly the rules of fermionic modes, $v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}$. [[c:tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors]]
t:transport.transport-algorithm>tower.wi:
The next result counts how much of this quantum structure each floor can hold. [[t]]

The number of modes realisable by vectors is the Witt index, \[ \min(p,q) \] and along the tower it is $\min(p,q) + k$, one more per rung. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]]
i:walls:
Real geometries can degenerate in some places and not in others, so the repair has to be made locally, along a wall. [[t]]

The standing tameness assumption fixes what is allowed: a smooth closed wall, exactly one direction losing its length at each point, and that length vanishing at a linear rate. [[c:sheaf.tameness]]
t:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity>shea:
With that assumption in place, the repair can be carried right up to the wall. [[t]]

On the physical side the completed form is nondegenerate of signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ at every point, including the wall, so every fibre is \[ \Cl(2,4) \cong \Mat_4(\HH) \] in the physical case. [[c:sheaf.one-sided-completion]]
i:singularity:
The centre of a black hole is the first physical place where the repair is put to work. [[t]]

Approaching it, the gravitational field grows without bound, but once that growth is divided out the field settles to a limit that is degenerate. [[c:singularity.degeneration-exactly]]
t:sheaf.one-sided-completion>singularity:
The question is which kind of obstruction this degeneration turns out to be. [[t]]

It is type N, a null direction without a partner, and type C cannot occur, because \[ p - q = -2 \equiv 6 \pmod 8 \] makes $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ simple. [[c:singularity.type-n-only-type-n]]
i:einstein: To say anything about gravity itself, the series needs Einstein's equations in a form that lives naturally in the enlarged space. [[t]]
t:singularity.type-n-only-type-n>interio:
The next result supplies such a form. [[t]]

In Gauge Theory Gravity on flat spacetime, the vacuum field equations hold exactly when the null scale tractor $I_g = \nInf$ is parallel for the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field. [[c:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations]]
i:descent: After working upstairs one has to come back down, and any return journey must lose something. [[c:transport.door-one-way]] This section says what is lost and what the loss means. [[t]]
t:interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equatio:
The first result identifies the way down with a familiar operation. [[t]]

Descent is the average over fermion parity, \[ E(x) \;=\; \tfrac12\bigl(x + \alpha(x)\bigr) \] whose kernel is exactly the adjoined ladder sector. [[c:singularity.descent-parity-average]]
t:singularity.descent-parity-average>sin:
That leaves the question of where the missing partner of a mixed state comes from. [[t]]

In the state's own representation the partner is the commutant, and for a Gibbs state the cyclic vector is the thermofield double. [[c:singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant]]
i:thermality: The series next asks whether the modes it finds at the black-hole boundary can be hot, in the sense that Hawking described. [[t]]
t:singularity.purity-output-partner-comm:
The thermal case of that construction now meets the black hole directly. [[t]]

At inverse temperature \[ \beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa \] the boundary modes have a state thermal for the boost clock, and within the quasi-free class it is unique, its two-point data forced. [[c:hawking.i-state]]
i:dark-energy: The cosmological constant enters through the frozen point, a fixed direction in an enlarged conformal space whose length the constant sets. [[c:dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry]] One of the earlier results used here rests on an assumed principle rather than a proof. [[c:dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem]]
t:hawking.i-state>dark-energy.frozen-poi:
From heat the tour turns to gravity on the largest scale. [[t]]

Where $\Lambda \neq 0$, the frozen point supplies the Stelle-West vector, so gravity's action makes sense where the metric degenerates. [[c:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector]]
i:mass: The tour now turns from gravity to matter, using twistors, in which a single twistor describes a massless particle travelling at light speed. [[c:mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula]]
t:dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-:
The first question about matter is where its mass comes from. [[t]]

A single conformal spinor carries the null momentum \[ p_{AA'} = \pi_{A}\bar\pi_{A'} \] and is massless, so mass first appears for a system of two. [[c:mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula]]
i:standard-model: Next the tour asks which forces such a massive composite would feel. [[t]]
t:mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-:
Looking inside the smallest massive composite answers that question. [[t]]

Two conformal spinors of three pairs each have automorphisms $(U(2) \times U(3))/U(1)$, with Lie algebra \[ \su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1) \] the Standard Model's exactly. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]]
i:generations:
The next question is why matter might repeat itself in families. [[t]]

Here Hypothesis (S), an assumption about how the slots of a composite behave, is needed, and several of the framework's particle-physics results hold only if it does. [[c:standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics]] In particular, everything said about charged leptons depends on it. [[c:families.imported-one-derived-generation-hypothesis-s]]
t:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-m:
Allowing a composite more than two twistors leads to a simple count of choices. [[t]]

The faces, three of them under the three-spinor bound, carry identical content, because the permutations $S_{3}$ of the slots carry each face's copy onto every other. [[c:families.three-identical-families-mixing-shared-slots]]
i:neutrinos:
Neutrinos are where the framework comes closest to numbers that experiments can check. [[t]]

The account assumes that neutrinos carry a Majorana mass at a very high scale, which nothing in the framework yet shows forming. [[c:neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale]] The family picture it builds on is itself still a conjecture. [[c:neutrino.imported-indifference-faces-democratic-alignment-rank]]
t:families.three-identical-families-mixi:
Treating the families even-handedly has a sharp consequence for neutrino masses. [[t]]

The Dirac mass matrix is democratic, $\mD = d\,\J$, with the single eigenvalue $m_{D} = 3d$, so the seesaw gives the normal ordering. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]
i:dark-matter: The account of matter ends with matter we cannot see. [[t]] The answer rests on postulates, not proofs, about how the origin of the universe treats its hidden sectors. [[c:dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point]]
t:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-:
Swapping the roles of time and space gives a second world to set beside our own. [[t]]

Every input of the Standard Model chain is invariant under the reversal \[ (p,q) \mapsto (q,p) \] which carries $(1,3)$ to the mirror's $(3,1)$, so the mirror has the same gauge algebra and the same generation. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]]
i:one-relation:
The tour closes by stepping back to the single rule behind everything. [[t]]

That rule, $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$, can be read as geometry or as the rule obeyed by fermions, though only at the level of structure. [[c:one-relation.two-presentations]]
t:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one>one-:
A last result counts the quantum structure in two ways. [[t]]

The real and complex capacities are \[ r_{\R}(p,q) = \min(p,q), \qquad r_{\C}(p,q) = \lfloor d/2 \rfloor \] and for spacetime $(1,3)$ they are $1$ and $2$. [[c:one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences]]
conclusion:
The thread of the tour is one move, made again and again. [[t]] Division fails along null directions, so the space is enlarged by a pair of new directions, one of each sign. [[c:transport.minimality]] The work is done in the larger setting and the answer is brought back, noting where it cannot come back. [[c:transport.transport-algorithm]]

At the centre of a non-rotating black hole that move supplies the missing partner. [[c:singularity.type-n-only-type-n]] Its boundary modes then carry a thermal state at the Hawking temperature whose occupation numbers are derived rather than chosen. [[c:hawking.i-state]] On the matter side, the same algebra yields the symmetry of the strong, weak and hypercharge forces. [[c:standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite]]

Not all of this is proved from nothing, and the assumptions are part of the picture. [[t]] The repair along a wall assumes the degeneration is tame. [[c:sheaf.tameness]] The family results assume Hypothesis (S) about slot statistics. [[c:standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics]]

The neutrino results assume that the framework realises a heavy Majorana mass, which is left for later work. [[c:neutrino.m-framework-realises-majorana-term-scale]] The sharp total neutrino mass further assumes that the lightest neutrino gets almost no mass. [[c:neutrino.h-second-stage-hierarchical]]

The mirror world assumes a single shared origin for every hidden sector. [[c:dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point]] It also assumes that only sectors related by a reflection are forced to match. [[c:dark-matter.p2-indifference]] That the matter excess is imprinted equally in the two mirror sectors is proved for the mirror copy, not assumed. [[c:dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one]]

Under these assumptions the framework makes claims that can fail. [[t]] It predicts that the three neutrino masses add up to about 0.059 eV, with the normal ordering. [[c:pred.neutrino-mass-sum-floor]] It expects no neutrinoless double-beta signal at next-generation sensitivity, so a clear signal would count against it. [[c:pred.no-neutrinoless-double-beta]] It predicts no echoes after black holes merge, and a single confirmed echo would refute it. [[c:scrambling.no-echo-prediction-registered]]
